chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sa'id al-A'raj,
he said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about a jar that holds one hundred ratls — an uqiyyah of blood falls into it: may I drink from it and perform wudu? He said: No.

key_terms.أُوقِيَّةٌ: uqiyyah — a small traditional unit of measure (approx. 40 g); the quantity of blood in question
key_terms.الْجَرَّةِ: large clay jar/vessel used for storing water — the subject of the jurisprudential query
key_terms.دَمٍ: blood — classified as a major ritual impurity (najasah 'ayniyyah) in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.رِطْلٍ: ratl — a traditional unit of weight (approx. 340 g); 100 ratls is a substantial but sub-kur volume of water

ai.seo_question: If an uqiyyah of blood falls into a jar holding one hundred ratls of water, is it permitted to drink from it or use it for wudu according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Sa'id al-A'raj posed a question to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) about a large clay jar containing 100 ratls of water into which a small measure (uqiyyah) of blood had fallen, asking whether the water remained suitable for drinking and wudu. The Imam's terse, unequivocal 'No' establishes the legal ruling that even a small quantity of blood renders water of this volume (below the kur threshold) ritually impure (najis), invalidating its use for both consumption and ritual purification.
